proof_summary: Writing \(M=p^e u\), the proof splits the numerator difference \(B(M)-pB(M/p)\) by whether \(p\mid k\) and proves divisibility by \(p^{4e}\): the coprime-index part uses block cancellation of inverse-square sums and a peeled binomial-ratio recurrence, while the divisible-index part uses paired product expansions and valuation bounds for binomial cube differences. Since \(B(M)=M a(M)\), canceling the \(p^e\)-part of \(M\) yields divisibility by \(p^{3e}\), which suffices because \(e=v_p(np^r)\ge r\).
